subject: Stormburst POC traffic handshake & ownership
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Klein <alex.klein@nimbushealth.com>, Leslie Park <leslie.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stormburst POC traffic handshake & ownership

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the Nimbus team. Quick recap + next steps so everyone has a single source of truth. Please flag any corrections.

Recap of the workload profile you described:
- Steady-state RPS: ~8-12 RPS (user-facing inference).
- Burst behavior: recurring short bursts ~5–10 minutes; observed peaks up to 400–500 RPS during marketing pushes.
- Token lengths: prompts ~30–60 tokens (median ~40); model responses vary, avg ~160 tokens, worst-case up to ~420 tokens.
- Concurrency target: 16–24 concurrent sessions (mostly short-lived).
- Latency target: soft target p95 < 300ms for UI flows.

Proposed owners for POC/trial:
- Redwood trial ops: Ben Carter (kickoff, environment, capacity)
- Redwood telemetry & SLAs: Monica Patel (metrics, dashboards, alerts)
- Redwood escalation/contract: Rishi Malhotra (SLA + commercial)
- Nimbus technical lead: Alex Klein (traffic artifacts, test data, internal sched)

Immediate asks from Nimbus:
1) Share sample traffic artifacts (schema or small log export) or confirm we can generate a representative synthetic load generator. (Attachment: traffic_sample_schema.json)
2) Confirm whether the 400–500RPS bursts are sustained for 5 min or 20+ min — you said they often come in short spikes during campaigns; we need precise burst length to size warm capacity.
3) Legal/commercial question: do you need data residency or special controls? (I believe you said US-only.)

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- Kickoff meeting: target week of Mar 21 (please propose available slots)
- Synthetic load ingestion or sample upload: by Mar 23
- Baseline trial run (3 full days): Mar 24–26
- Sign-off and recommended config: by Mar 31

Success metrics (draft):
- Performance: p95 latency under steady-state <= 300ms; during burst windows p95 <= 600ms with no more than 1–2 degradation events/hour.
- Reliability: error rate <= 1% (5xx/timeout) across trial window.
- Cost/ops: token cost and concurrency within agreed budget envelope (we'll estimate once we have token distributions).
- Quality: pass rate on your verification prompt set >= 90%.

Next steps for Alex/Leslie: please attach a 24–72 hour sampling of representative traffic or confirm we should proceed with a synthetic generator that matches the numbers above.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Stormburst POC traffic handshake & ownership

Thanks Mina — helpful summary. Couple clarifications from our side:
- The 400–500 RPS bursts are typically 4–7 minutes; very rarely exceed 10 minutes. They are concentrated shortly after push notifications (campaign windows).
- Steady-state is closer to 6–8 RPS average; I rounded up on the call.
- Token distribution: ~85% of responses under 200 tokens, but we have a tail of ~5% between 300–420 tokens.

Two questions:
1) How does Redwood handle cold-starts for KV/cache-heavy prompts? We have some flows that rely on personalized context and might see higher initial latency.
2) For telemetry, we will need per-route token counts and a way to tie latency regressions back to prompt types. Can Monica propose a minimal telemetry contract?

We will pull a 48-hour sample for you (anonymized) and aim to upload it by Tue, Mar 16 COB. Also confirming Nimbus is US-only for data.

— Alex
Alex Klein
Platform Lead, Nimbus Health
alex.klein@nimbushealth.com

Subject: Re: Stormburst POC traffic handshake & ownership

Appreciate the clarifications, Alex — that's exactly the level of detail we need. Quick answers and a recommended config for the POC: 

Cold-starts / KV cache:
- We'll provision a small warm pool of workers to keep commonly used contexts loaded during campaign windows. For flows with high personalization, we recommend a short warm-up window (30–60s) prior to high-volume pushes.
- Redwood's runtime maintains per-session KV caching; first request in a session may be slower (~1s) if not warm, subsequent requests should hit cache. We'll include a pre-warm script as part of trial ops.

Telemetry / minimal contract (Monica):
- Per-route p50/p95/p99 latencies, request/response token counts, error counts, and 1-min RPS.
- Correlation keys: route id + custom tag (we'll provide instructions to tag test traffic).
- Delivery: shared dashboard + nightly export to your S3.

Recommended POC config:
- Batching window: aggressive batching up to 20ms for steady-state; dynamic reduction during bursts to preserve latency.
- Warm pool size: sized to cover expected burst concurrency (we'll propose initial pool for 400 RPS peaks).
- Model variant: start with a quantized variant for cost-bound tests; we can switch to higher-fidelity model for quality checks.

Draft success criteria (refined):
- p95 latency <= 300ms steady-state; p95 <= 600ms during burst windows with no more than 1% request failures.
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate on your verification prompts measured across a 24-hour sweep.
- Operational: telemetry and dashboard available within 48 hours of ingest.

Proposed timeline (finalized):
- Mar 16: Nimbus uploads 48h anonymized sample (thanks).
- Mar 18: Redwood provides synthetic generator + config recommendations.
- Mar 21 (week of) — 30-min kickoff, proposed 10:00 AM PT on Mar 21.
- Mar 23: Synthetic ingestion / sample run.
- Mar 24–26: Baseline runs and telemetry collection.
- Mar 31: Trial sign-off or recommended adjustments.

Attachments: poc-success-metrics-draft.md (attached)

Ben — can you take lead on scheduling the kickoff and creating the Meet invite? Rishi — I'll send a short note on SLAs and any commercial flags after we confirm scope.

Thanks — Mina
